reviews.text: Celestia is a modular blockchain for data availability, allowing other chains to use it for storage. Launched in 2023, it uses proof-of-stake and blob tech for scalability. In 2025, it’s key for rollups like EigenDA. The team is research-focused. It’s foundational but not user-facing.

Celestia is a blockchain data infrastructure network based on the modular blockchain concept. celestia only provides the consensus+data availability layers(DA).  Transaction execution leaves smart contract execution to other chains/rollups. Developers can build their own blockchain and rollup using Celestia's data and security layer(block space as a service (BaaS)). The network's native coin is TIA. Its supply is 1,156,152,362. Rollups and chains pay blobspace/DA fees (in TIA) to publish their data on Celestia. By staking TIA, they contribute to network security and have a say in governance through staking. Tia's goal is to break down the comprehensive, yet cumbersome and expensive structure of blockchains to create more scalable, private light chains and rollups.

Celestia is a “modular” blockchain that provides data availability and consensus to other chains. It separates the data layer from execution, letting developers launch rollups or custom chains while Celestia handles reliable data storage. In Nov 2025, Celestia deployed its Matcha upgrade to increase data capacity: larger block sizes, from 8 MB to 128 MB (16x) and token inflation was cut from 5% to 2.5%. Projects like Doma (on-chain domain trading), Hibachi Exchange and others have chosen Celestia for its scalable data layer. The token TIA was airdropped to the community in October 2023.

Celestia is a blockchain infrastructure that specializes in providing cheap scalable and decentralized Data availability for modular blockchain using Data availability sampling mechanism. The project was founded by experienced team members from Celetia Labs backed by huge funding from top tier VCs like Bain Capital Crypto, Polychain Capital, Dragonfly, Binance Labs and Placeholder. Celestia has secured strategic partnerships with Rollup Frameworks like Rollkit allowing developers to build sovereign rollups on Celestia and the Cosmos SDK. Moreover, Celestia employs good security measures including multiple third audits and a high reward bug bounty program with maximum bounty of up to $750,0000. The governance and utility token of Celetia $TIA is managed by DAO. 
In my opinion, Celestia has potential even though it is associated with some risks which includes 51% attack, DAS complex and primitive nature and competition from other data availability solutions.

Celestia feels like a big picture blockchain infrastructure: it essentially provides the data and consensus layer so other chains like rollups don’t have to. That modular idea is really elegant you can launch a sovereign chain simply by publishing your data here. To me it’s a logical evolution if blockchains split work layers. The only catch I see is that it’s niche: its value hinges on many projects choosing to use it. There’s talk that modular systems could fragment if competitors arise, which Celestia’s team acknowledges is a challenge.

Celestia is a modular blockchain project that focuses on scalability and flexibility. Unlike traditional blockchains, which handle both consensus and execution in a single layer, Celestia separates these two functions. This modular design allows developers to build custom blockchains that can scale more effectively while maintaining decentralization. By enabling different applications to operate on their own specialized chains, Celestia aims to address the scalability challenges faced by more monolithic blockchain structures, positioning itself as an innovative solution in the blockchain space.
